title: QUIC server first-flight x25519 key-share compatibility architecture
purpose: Define the narrow server-side managed TLS compatibility branch that accepts an advertised usable first-flight x25519 ClientHello key share without broad TLS group negotiation or interop support promotion.
design_summary: The transcript parser treats x25519 as a second explicitly supported server first-flight key-share branch. It continues to ignore unsupported hybrid key-share entries, rejects duplicate, malformed, or unadvertised x25519 entries, and still emits the existing secp256r1 HelloRetryRequest only when no usable first-flight supported share exists and the peer advertised secp256r1. The key schedule keeps the existing P-256 client profile and public support boundary, adds a server-owned x25519 ephemeral key pair backed by the repo-local RFC 7748 helper for ServerHello construction and ECDHE secret derivation, and selects the ServerHello key_share group from the parsed ClientHello step. This avoids the quic-go first-flight HRR blocker without adding hybrid groups, broad group negotiation, client-side x25519, HTTP/3, anti-replay, or interop support promotion.
edge_cases_and_constraints: A ClientHello x25519 key share is accepted only when supported_groups also advertises x25519.
Duplicate x25519 key_share entries fail deterministically instead of allowing ambiguous selection.
Malformed x25519 key_share lengths fail deterministically.
Unsupported hybrid key shares are ignored and are never selected.
The existing secp256r1 HRR fallback remains the only HelloRetryRequest branch.
The client-generated ClientHello and public IsSupported boundary remain unchanged.
alternatives_considered: Continue forcing HelloRetryRequest for peers that send x25519. Rejected because the zerortt runner proof shows quic-go closes 0-RTT after HRR even when a usable first-flight x25519 key share is present.
Add general TLS group negotiation. Rejected because the approved slice is only a bounded CRT compatibility branch for a checked first-flight group.
Accept unsupported hybrid key shares. Rejected because that would widen cryptographic support beyond available proof and platform ownership.
risks: Treating x25519 parser acceptance as broad client-side x25519 support would overstate the support boundary.
Selecting x25519 without verifying supported_groups would accept unadvertised key-share material.
Treating the repo-local RFC 7748 helper as a general-purpose constant-time crypto primitive would overstate this bounded compatibility slice.
Promoting the interop zerortt cell before live runner proof would hide remaining runtime or harness failures.

supplemental_sections.heading: Scope Boundaries
supplemental_sections.content:
- Server-side first-flight x25519 only.
- No hybrid group support.
- No client-side x25519 ClientHello generation.
- No public API or IsSupported widening.
- No HTTP/3 scope.
- No interop promotion without a separate live runner proof.
